title: Audit ingest: hotspot resilience, partition rebalancer, and cost-throttle playbook
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Background: Recent incidents (INC-2026-003, see links) exposed two recurring pain points in the audit ingest pipeline: 1) short-lived hotspots from customer bursts that overload single partitions and degrade query latency for everyone, and 2) unbounded retention growth for high-volume customers that drives storage cost spikes. Scope: design and implement a resilient ingest-side architecture and operational playbook that combines adaptive partition rebalancing, per-customer cost throttles, and retention automation. Out of scope: long-term cold storage archival format changes (handled in ENG-41800). Goals: 1) eliminate cascading latency impact caused by per-partition hotspots, 2) cap predictable daily storage ingestion per-customer with graceful backpressure and telemetry, and 3) implement retention tier automation (hot/warm/cold) tied to cost guardrails and query SLOs.
acceptance_criteria: Partition rebalancer service deployed to staging and can move partitions without downtime
Hotspot detection alerting implemented with < 60s detection for sustained tail latency > 99th percentile threshold
Per-customer daily ingest cap enforced with soft/ hard modes and documented billing signals
Retention automation policy can migrate indexes to warm/cold tiers and reclaim storage within SLA
Runbook and playbook published in Confluence and reviewed by Security and SRE
progress_updates: 2026-02-28: Kickoff meeting with SRE, Storage, and Security. Captured incident timelines and SLOs. Assigned owners for rebalancer prototype and cost-throttle design.
2026-03-03: Prototype decision: hybrid partitioning - time-bucket primary + customer-shard secondary. Rationale: reduces partition churn while allowing per-customer isolation for high-volume tenants.
2026-03-05: Trade-off discussion with Storage: use of hash vs range partitioning. Chose hash-on-customer-id for even distribution and easier rebalancer logic. Documented in design doc.

2026-03-07: Implemented early hotspot detector in staging (simple moving-window QPS + 99th latency). Detected two synthetic hotspots; rebalancer simulation moved affected shards with < 5s interruption in ingest path.

2026-03-10: Security review kickoff. RBAC v2 impacts surfaced: rebalancer needs a service principal with scoped admin permissions. Working with Security to limit scope to partition-metadata endpoints only.
2026-03-12: Design doc v1 posted; tests added for partition movement race conditions. Next: build cost-throttle enforcement and integrate billing signals into alerts.
decision_summary: Adopt a hybrid partitioning strategy: time-bucketed index shards with customer-hash subshards. Implement a central 'partition-rebalancer' service that watches hotspot signals and triggers shard migration. Enforce per-customer ingest caps via gateway-level soft/hard throttles; soft mode emits rich telemetry and pre-warning webhooks, hard mode drops or rejects excess events. Retention automation will be TTL-driven with adaptive windows based on customer class and query heat. RBAC v2 will restrict rebalancer and billing operations to narrowly scoped service principals.
tasks: Design and document hybrid partition schema (time + customer-hash)
Build partition-rebalancer prototype (Leader election, plan execution, safe move)
Hotspot detection engine (thresholds, hysteresis, alerting hooks)
Gateway integration for per-customer ingest throttle (soft/hard modes)
Retention automation controller (move to warm/cold, compact, delete)
RBAC v2 service principal and least-privilege policy for rebalancer
E2E tests for partition moves under load and recovery scenarios
Billing integration: surface daily ingestion usage and policy hits to billing pipeline
notes: Operability concerns: moving partitions must preserve ordering guarantees for a given customer id key prefix. We'll implement a cutover window with ephemeral buffering and KV cache flush semantics. Cost control policy will default to 'soft' for 30 days post-launch to avoid false positives on newly onboarded customers.
